candidates.title: Compare product-specific tax cases before checkout

demandEvidence.chore: Calculate product-specific tax amounts before checkout and record GST and PST accurately in order records and reports.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: Calculate the correct tax amounts before payment, without requiring draft orders, manual adjustments or additional invoices.

ease.reason: A synthetic case table is possible, but tax rules and correct calculations are not supported by implementation evidence.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: wholesale retailers may pay for fewer manual checkout adjustments; this request proves no buyer intent or payment.

feasibility.reason: A four-week calculator mock is possible, but correct jurisdiction and exemption rules are unresolved dependencies inside the output.

autonomy.reason: A draft can flag supplied cases, while a qualified person must verify tax treatment and authorize any use.

evidence.reason: The retained task and context spans identify checkout calculation and record accuracy needs; no implementation or corroboration is supplied.

experimentPlan.output: A review sheet comparing operator-entered product, customer exemption and tax inputs with an independently supplied expected amount, flagging mismatches without calculating production tax.
inputs: Expected tax amount from a qualified reviewer
experimentPlan.trigger: A person submits one synthetic checkout case for review.
steps: Collect the synthetic case and the reviewer-provided expected amount.
Apply only the operator-entered rule to produce a draft comparison.
Flag missing fields or a mismatch for human review.
Save the case and reviewer decision in a local test sheet.
experimentPlan.acceptanceCheck: For each test case, verify that the comparison flags a deliberately mismatched entered amount and does not present its own result as authoritative tax advice.
experimentPlan.humanBoundary: A qualified person supplies rules and expected amounts, reviews every discrepancy, and decides any real tax treatment; no live Shopify write or tax advice is proposed.
unverified: Whether available inputs fully represent product-specific GST/PST rules
Whether the comparison is useful across real businesses
No live Shopify integration or tax correctness is established

candidates.reason: Assessed from the assigned discussion. The proposed student experiment is narrow; provisional mean is below 6, so it is recorded in rejected.

candidates.title: Prepare game-test CSV logs for review

demandEvidence.chore: Enter mobile game-test measurements in notes, export a CSV, paste it into a Google Sheet, and avoid processing the same file twice.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: Right now I type it into a notes app during the session, then later export a CSV from that app and paste it into a Google Sheet.

ease.reason: The supplied n8n references support CSV row extraction and duplicate comparison (5c2bf4e7df8c3ec325ba2e74; f1662b0ceb942474f83a8108), but not phone intake.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: independent game testers may pay for cleaner log imports; the post establishes no buying intent or payment.

feasibility.reason: A synthetic CSV flow is bounded and both extraction and deduplication are documented by the cited n8n sources; live trigger setup remains unverified.

autonomy.reason: Rows can be extracted and compared, but a person must choose a stable key, verify results and import them; duplicate removal capability is documented by f1662b0ceb942474f83a8108.

evidence.reason: The retained context names four logged measures, notes-to-CSV-to-Sheets handling, and a trigger firing zero or twice; recurrence beyond this user is unknown.

experimentPlan.output: A reviewable table of parsed game-test rows with repeated rows flagged before a person imports the CSV into a Sheet.
inputs: Synthetic CSV with battery, temperature, frame-drop and note columns
experimentPlan.trigger: A tester manually supplies an exported CSV for a review run.
steps: Read the supplied CSV into row objects using the documented n8n extraction node.
Check required columns and mark incomplete rows.
Compare selected fields against prior test rows using the documented duplicate-removal node.
Produce a review table of new, repeated and incomplete rows.
Have a person verify matches and import approved rows into Sheets.
experimentPlan.acceptanceCheck: Use a small synthetic CSV containing a repeated row and one missing measurement; confirm the report flags both and preserves the original values for review.
experimentPlan.humanBoundary: The tester exports and submits files, selects matching fields, checks flagged rows and imports approved data; phone upload triggers and live Sheet writes are outside scope.
unverified: Whether chosen fields identify the same test event reliably
Whether the free n8n setup can run the desired phone-to-drive trigger
No actual workflow execution or external endpoint is established

candidates.title: Review recovery gaps in agent runs

demandEvidence.chore: Write checkpoint and recovery logic and handle idempotency for agent workflows.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: But devs need to write checkpointers, recovery logic, and deal with idempotency by theirselves.

ease.reason: A supplied incident table can be reviewed manually, but no supplied implementation reference supports checkpoint or safe retry behavior.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: teams building agent workflows may pay for recovery reviews; the post establishes no buyer intent or payment.

feasibility.reason: A four-week synthetic failure review is bounded, but reliable recovery logic and safe side-effect handling are unresolved core capabilities.

autonomy.reason: The proposal can organize failure cases, but a developer must design, test and authorize recovery behavior.

evidence.reason: The post names three engineering burdens but provides no concrete scenario, inputs, recurrence or corroboration.

experimentPlan.output: A human-reviewed recovery case sheet that maps a supplied agent failure description to missing checkpoint and duplicate-side-effect questions.
inputs: List of external side effects in the test scenario
experimentPlan.trigger: A developer submits one synthetic failed-run case for review.
steps: Record the supplied failure point and checkpoint history.
List side effects that may already have occurred.
Flag unanswered questions about replay safety and idempotency.
Draft questions for a developer to resolve before any retry.
Have a developer approve or reject a proposed recovery approach.
experimentPlan.acceptanceCheck: For a synthetic failure with one completed external side effect and a missing checkpoint, confirm the sheet flags replay risk and does not recommend an automatic retry.
experimentPlan.humanBoundary: A developer supplies scenario facts, determines correct checkpoint semantics, verifies side effects and authorizes any retry; no agent execution or recovery is proposed.
unverified: Which checkpoint and replay semantics apply to any particular agent
Whether proposed questions help teams solve their failures
No recovery implementation, external endpoint, or successful retry is evidenced

candidates.title: Compare ad and Shopify purchase exports

demandEvidence.chore: Export daily purchases from Ads Manager and daily Shopify orders for the same 30-day period, then investigate differences including duplicate counting.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: In Shopify, export daily orders for the same 30 days, Online Store channel only, without test and cancelled orders.

ease.reason: A person can supply two exports for a comparison, but no supplied reference supports live account access or attribution analysis.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: small online shops may pay for a repeatable discrepancy review; the post establishes no purchase intent or payment.

feasibility.reason: A four-week synthetic comparison is feasible, while attribution settings and causes of gaps still require expert interpretation.

autonomy.reason: The proposed report can align daily totals and flag large changes, but a person must inspect causes and make any tracking changes.

evidence.reason: The retained spans give aligned 30-day export instructions and examples of expected differences and duplicate events, but only one discussion supports demand.

experimentPlan.output: A daily comparison table of operator-supplied Ads Manager and Shopify exports, with unusually large gaps flagged for human investigation.
inputs: Synthetic Ads Manager daily purchase export
Synthetic Shopify Online Store daily order export
Operator-selected date range and attribution setting
experimentPlan.trigger: A shop operator supplies two exports for the same chosen date range.
steps: Check that both files cover matching dates and the selected channel/settings.
Align rows by date and preserve each original total.
Calculate the difference and mark missing dates or unusually large changes.
Attach a short explanation checklist without assigning a cause.
Have a person inspect tracking settings and confirm any finding.
experimentPlan.acceptanceCheck: On synthetic exports with matching totals, one missing date and one deliberate doubled value, confirm that the table identifies the mismatched dates without claiming why they differ.
experimentPlan.humanBoundary: The operator exports and reviews data, confirms settings, and investigates causes; the proposal does not access accounts, identify attribution truth, or change tracking.
unverified: Which gap size deserves review for a given shop
Whether settings and export schemas remain consistent
No live Meta or Shopify connection, external endpoint, or verified diagnosis is established
